pharm: Imidazole antifungal that inhibits fungal ergosterol biosynthesis, disrupting cell-membrane integrity; applied topically with low systemic absorption.
quick: Apply to affected and surrounding skin once or twice daily (once daily for pityriasis versicolor)
Former category B; use only if clearly needed (no adequate human studies)
Excreted in human milk; use with caution in nursing women
Clinical response; local irritation at application site
summary: Oxiconazole nitrate is a topical imidazole antifungal indicated for tinea pedis, tinea cruris, and tinea corporis caused by Trichophyton rubrum, Trichophyton mentagrophytes, or Epidermophyton floccosum, and for tinea (pityriasis) versicolor due to Malassezia furfur. It works by inhibiting fungal ergosterol synthesis and is applied to the skin once or twice daily, with very low systemic absorption. It is for external use only - not for ophthalmic or intravaginal use. Tinea corporis/cruris and pityriasis versicolor are treated for 2 weeks and tinea pedis for 1 month to limit recurrence. Side effects are local (pruritus, burning, irritation).
indications: Topical treatment of tinea pedis, tinea cruris, and tinea corporis due to Trichophyton rubrum, Trichophyton mentagrophytes, or Epidermophyton floccosum
Topical treatment of tinea (pityriasis) versicolor due to Malassezia furfur

dosage.c: Tinea pedis, tinea corporis, tinea cruris
dosage.d: Apply to affected and immediately surrounding areas once or twice daily
dosage.n: Treat tinea corporis/cruris for 2 weeks; treat tinea pedis for 1 month to reduce recurrence
Treat for 2 weeks; pigment normalization may take months

admin: For external (topical) use only - avoid eyes, nose, mouth, and other mucous membranes
Wash hands after applying to the affected area
Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms improve
Avoid occlusive dressings unless directed by the prescriber
If no improvement after 2-4 weeks (or sooner if worsening), reassess the diagnosis
moa: Oxiconazole is an imidazole derivative whose antifungal activity derives primarily from inhibition of ergosterol biosynthesis, a sterol critical for fungal cell-membrane integrity. Loss of ergosterol disrupts the membrane and is fungicidal/fungistatic against susceptible dermatophytes and Malassezia furfur. Systemic absorption after topical application is low (less than 0.3% of an applied dose recovered in urine).

absolute: Hypersensitivity to oxiconazole or any component of the formulation
relative: Application to eyes or mucous membranes (not for ophthalmic or intravaginal use)
monitor: Local skin reactions (irritation, burning, itching, blistering)

preg: Animal reproduction studies (oral doses up to 27-57 times the human dose) showed no fetal harm, but there are no adequate, well-controlled human studies (formerly Pregnancy Category B). Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Oxiconazole is excreted in human milk; exercise caution when administered to a nursing woman.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed; systemic absorption after topical application is minimal.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed; systemic absorption after topical application is minimal.

interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference. Potential drug interactions have not been systematically evaluated.

monitoring: Local skin tolerance (irritation, burning, blistering, oozing)
counsel: Apply a thin layer to the affected area and a little of the surrounding skin as directed
This cream is for the skin only - keep it away from your eyes, nose, and mouth
Use it for the full time prescribed, even if the rash looks better
Tell your doctor if the area gets more irritated, or if there is no improvement after 2-4 weeks
pk: Acts locally in the skin from first application
Penetrates epidermis and corium; systemic absorption low (<0.3% of dose in urine)
Once- or twice-daily dosing maintains skin levels
pearls: For external use only - never apply to the eyes or use intravaginally
Treat tinea pedis for a full month (vs 2 weeks for tinea corporis/cruris) to limit recurrence
In pityriasis versicolor, skin pigment may take months to normalize even after the fungus is cleared
Rarely effective indications occur in children under 12, but it may be used in pediatric patients
Reassess the diagnosis if there is no response after 2-4 weeks
missed: If you forget an application, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next application, skip the missed one - do not apply a double amount.
overdose: Topical overdose is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity given minimal absorption; excessive application may cause local irritation. There are no reports of overdose in humans with the cream or lotion. If accidentally ingested, provide supportive care.
